match.reason: The new point is a broad list of strategies (training, motivation, leadership change, redeploying resources, innovation, technology, cost cutting, lean production), and no bank point covers that whole set: performance management is about the review process, leadership style covers only one strategy, and operations and profitability cover narrower ideas.

draft.title: Strategies to improve performance
card: Managers use strategies to lift a business's performance, such as sales, profit, quality or productivity. The right choice depends on the problem the business faces.
People strategies
staff training builds skills, staff motivation lifts effort, and a change of management style alters how managers lead and make decisions.
Resource and product strategies
redeploying resources moves them to better uses. Innovation brings new products or methods. New technology can speed up work or cut errors.
Cost strategies
cost cutting lowers expenses. Lean production reduces waste, such as extra stock or idle time, while keeping quality.
draft.remember: Match the strategy to the problem: people, resources and products, or costs.

a.q: A bakery's profit is falling because it throws out a lot of unsold stock and wastes ingredients. Which strategy targets this problem most directly?
opts: Lean production to reduce waste
Staff motivation to lift effort
Innovation to launch a new product
A change of management style
a.why: The problem is waste, and lean production aims to reduce waste while keeping quality. Innovation might add sales, but it does not deal with the waste that is already happening.
a.clue: Which strategy is about cutting waste?

b.q: Priya manages a call centre in Geelong. Staff make many errors because they do not know the new billing system. Which strategy fits best?
opts: Staff training on the billing system
Cost cutting by reducing staff hours
Innovation by creating a new service
Redeploying staff to another business area
b.why: The errors come from missing skills, so training fixes the cause. Cost cutting might lower expenses, but it does nothing about the skills gap and could make errors worse.
b.clue: What is missing: skills, money or new products?

b.best: Staff training on the billing system

a.q: A bakery bakes far more loaves than it sells each day, and the leftover bread is thrown out each night. Which strategy targets this problem most directly?
opts: Lean production
Staff motivation
Innovation
A change of management style
a.why: Baking more than it sells leaves extra stock, and lean production aims to cut that kind of excess while keeping quality. Innovation might bring new sales, but it does not stop the bakery from making bread it never sells.
a.clue: Think about what the bakery makes but never sells.

b.q: Priya manages a call centre in Geelong. Staff make many errors because they were never shown how to use the new billing system. Which strategy fits best?
opts: Staff training for the customer service team
Cost cutting by reducing staff hours
Innovation by creating a new service
Redeploying staff to another business area
b.why: The errors come from missing skills, so training fixes the cause. Cost cutting might lower expenses, but it does nothing about the skills gap and could make errors worse.
b.clue: What is missing: skills, money or new products?

b.best: Staff training for the customer service team
